headline: Philippine Unemployment Falls to 5.3% in August
seoTitle: Philippine Unemployment Falls to 5.3% in August
seoDescription: PSA preliminary data put August 2026 unemployment at 5.3%, with 2.77 million jobless Filipinos and 49.79 million employed.
deck: The jobless count declined by about 375,000 from July, but the unemployment rate remained above August 2025.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: The Philippine unemployment rate fell to 5.3% in August 2026 from 6.0% in July, according to preliminary Labor Force Survey results released by the Philippine Statistics Authority on October 7. The estimated number of unemployed Filipinos declined to 2.77 million from 3.14 million.
Employment increased by about 574,000 to 49.79 million, lifting the employment rate to 94.7%. The labor force numbered 52.56 million.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Agriculture and forestry added about 847,000 workers from July, which the PSA linked to the planting season. Construction and wholesale and retail trade also recorded gains. Public administration and defense, manufacturing, administrative and support services, information and communication, and fishing and aquaculture recorded the largest month-to-month declines.
About 5.9 million employed people were underemployed, meaning they wanted more work hours, an additional job or a job with longer hours.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The month-to-month improvement signals more work opportunities, but the 5.3% jobless rate was still above the 3.9% recorded in August 2025. Seasonal agriculture gains and underemployment make job quality and durability as important as the headline rate.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch whether employment gains persist beyond planting season, whether manufacturing recovers, and whether underemployment continues to ease in subsequent PSA releases.

The article labels the results preliminary and separates month-to-month improvement from the higher year-on-year unemployment rate.
